newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban report fighting as Masood pushes south.
newsitem.headline: Taleban report fighting as Masood pushes south.

text.p: The Taleban militia ruling Kabul said fighting continued on Saturday on the front line north of the capital with sporadic exchanges of fire as forces under fomrer government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood pushed south.
The Taleban also reported that a warplane which bombed the Afghan capital and killed three children last week was shot down as it flew back north.
A northern alliance between Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum and Masood has been battling towards Kabul for the past two weeks.
Taleban commanders said fighting continued on Friday night and Saturday morning on the front line 25 to 30 km (15 to 19 miles) north of Kabul.
"Masood launched a big offensive at 8 p.m. (1530 GMT) last night on our front lines on the new road," said Mullah Gul Mohammed, a divisional commander on the Taleban front line.
"We stopped it and they lost two tanks and four dead in the offensive."

He was referring to the road running up the eastern side of the Shamali valley. The so-called old road runs parallel up the western side. The mullah said alliance forces had made some gains on the old road.
"There was lots of fighting last night on the old road. Our information is that Masood's forces are advancing south and have taken some ground." he said.
Sporadic exchanges of artillery and rocket fire continued on Saturday morning and a Taleban artillery officer told Reuters that his guns were hitting alliance forces on the old road.
"Masood is trying to advance, so we are hitting his troop concentrations," he said.

The fighting between the Taleban, who control three quarters of the country, and the alliance has been deadlocked in a range of hills across the Shamali Valley for two weeks, with only small changes in the front line despite numerous attacks by alliance forces.

The official radio, renamed Radio Sharia after Islam's stern law the Taleban want to impose on Afghanistan, said the warplane was brought down by "special guided missiles" after its bombing run over Kabul on Thursday.
It said the pilot was killed when his plane was brought down over the Kohdaman mountains north of Kabul after he "bombed Kabul city's residential areas".
There was no independent confirmation of what would be the first known shooting down of a warplane since the Taleban took Kabul on September 27.
Dostum has conducted several air raids on Kabul over the past week, most aimed at the airport on the northeastern edge of the city which is used for both civilian and military traffic.
Although one of the first bombs landed at night in a city centre park, there had been no civilian casualties in the raids until Thursday.
Then one plane dropped two 250 kg (550 lb) bombs on a northwestern suburb, destroying two houses, killing three children and wounding seven people, some seriously.
Local people said the attack was probably aimed at a nearby military base. The raids on the airport have failed to damage it and it remains open to traffic.
